regional_gaps.Europe: Missing comparable city limits for parts of Belgium, the Ottoman Balkans, and western Russia; industrial conurbations require municipal separation.
regional_gaps.East Asia: Qing and Korean municipal totals and homogeneous boundaries are incomplete. Maritime Customs port districts can exceed the corresponding city.
regional_gaps.South Asia: Some princely jurisdictions and cantonments need smaller-unit returns. Combined civilian and military town counts do not establish a continuous urban footprint.
regional_gaps.Southeast Asia: Java city versus regency, Saigon versus Cholon, and Bangkok city versus province remain uneven. Burmese cities use the Indian census while their region is Southeast Asia.
regional_gaps.West Asia and North Africa: Province and registration totals must not stand in for cities. Some Moroccan and Arabian urban estimates are broad or disagree.
regional_gaps.Sub-Saharan Africa: Local counts often omit people and settlements. City limits for Yoruba and Hausa centres and urban counts in Portuguese and Ottoman territories are incomplete.
regional_gaps.North America: Primary returns are strongest for the US and Canada. Canadian province totals do not imply the presence or absence of a major city.
regional_gaps.Latin America and Caribbean: 1900–1905 city-specific returns are uneven. Separate federal districts, municipal rural hinterland and built-up settlements. Rio's 1900 return was annulled.
regional_gaps.Oceania: Australian comparisons combine cities and suburbs; New Zealand returns list principal towns and suburbs. Island-wide returns are not urban counts.
regional_gaps.Central Asia: 1897 Russian city returns cover some cities. Separate Bukhara and Khiva and avoid replacing absent counts with district totals.
